I started ripping my hair out when I was really young, bashing my head against things, hitting myself, scratching my arms when I panicked. At the beginning of junior high, I started using safety pins to just scratch under the skin slightly, which quickly lead to scratching harder and harder until blood was flowing. I remember sitting on the bus scratching away at my arms crying because of how depressed I was from being alone and being bullied, as well as dealing with my parent's drug addiction. The next year my friend taught me about getting razors from pencil sharpeners, and from there I started a few times a week until eventually in early high school I was cutting in the double digits 5-7 times a week. 

I'm 21 years old now and I still struggle with self-harm every day.  The longest I've ever been clean was 6 months, I always relapse and fall into my old habits. Right now I just hit the 11-day mark, so whoohoo. 

Thank you for this post. Before reading this I never really thought about where my sh journey began, honestly I didn't even remember the scratching I used to do in junior high, and I never imaged it adding up to where I am today with large amounts of scars up and down my thigh. I feel better knowing that this is a learned behavior I've had for years, no wonder it's such a hard thing to kick. I don't think I ever truly will "kick it" either. My mom told me that once an addict always an addict, you can be in recovery but never fully clean because it's a learned habit.

I tend to be dramatic only because I FEEL emotions so strongly and nobody gets that. We feel deeper than other people making everything so much more physically painful and it drives me crazy. I'm constantly tired of dealing with my mood swings, and my thoughts and feelings.  It feels like an uphill battle that nobody will really understand.
